My Journey

During my B.Tech in Computer Science, I discovered my passion for turning raw data into meaningful business insights. I started my journey with Advanced Excel, where I learned data analysis, Pivot Tables, Power Query, charts, and reporting. As my interest grew, I expanded my skills to SQL for querying and managing data, Power BI for building interactive dashboards and visualizations, and Python for data analysis and automation. Every project strengthened my analytical thinking and deepened my understanding of how data can solve real-world business problems.

Throughout my learning journey, I worked on several real-world projects, including IPL Data Analysis, Hospital Emergency Room Dashboard, Pizza Sales Analysis, and HR Analytics Dashboard. These projects helped me gain practical experience in data cleaning, data transformation, exploratory data analysis (EDA), dashboard development, KPI reporting, and business intelligence. My goal is to build a successful career as a Data Analyst, MIS Executive, Research Analyst, or Business Analyst, where I can use data to support better decision-making and create meaningful business value while continuously learning and growing.

Career Objective

To begin my career as a Data Analyst, MIS Executive, Research Analyst, or Business Analyst, where I can apply my skills in Advanced Excel, SQL, Power BI, and Python to analyze data, create insightful reports and dashboards, and support data-driven business decisions. I am eager to learn from experienced professionals, continuously enhance my analytical and technical skills, and contribute to organizational growth by delivering accurate, meaningful, and actionable insights.

What I've Built

My Projects

01
IPL Data Analysis (2008–2026)

I collected and merged IPL match data from 19 seasons covering 1,243 matches, 19 teams, and 60 venues into a single clean dataset using Excel. I performed data cleaning by removing duplicates, standardizing team names, and fixing date formats. I wrote SQL queries in MS SQL Server using GROUP BY, JOINS, RANK, DENSE_RANK, CTEs, Views, and Stored Procedures to extract meaningful team and season insights. I then built an interactive Power BI dashboard with 4 pages — Executive Summary, Team Analysis, Venue & City, and Player Analysis — using DAX measures. Key findings include Mumbai Indians leading with 155 wins, AB de Villiers winning 25 Player of the Match awards, and Mumbai hosting 187 matches across all seasons.

Excel SQL Power BI DAX
GitHub View Dashboard
02
Hospital Emergency Dashboard

I built an interactive monthly Excel dashboard to track key hospital KPIs including Total Patients, Average Wait Time, and Patient Satisfaction Score. I cleaned and transformed raw patient data using Power Query to ensure accurate and reliable reporting. The dashboard includes Pivot Tables and Pivot Charts to analyze patient flow by age group, gender, and department. I added month and year slicers for dynamic filtering to make MIS reporting easy and efficient. The project also summarizes admission status and department referrals to support better hospital management decisions.

Advanced Excel Power Query Pivot Tables Pivot Charts
GitHub View Dashboard
03
Pizza Sales Analysis

I analyzed pizza sales transaction data to extract meaningful business insights related to revenue, customer order patterns, and product performance. I wrote SQL queries to calculate key KPIs including Total Revenue, Average Order Value, Total Pizzas Sold, Total Orders, and Average Pizzas per Order. I performed sales trend analysis to identify daily and monthly order patterns and conducted revenue analysis by pizza category and size. I also identified the Top 5 and Bottom 5 performing pizzas by revenue, quantity sold, and total orders. I built an interactive Power BI dashboard to visualize all key metrics in a clear and easy-to-understand format. Key insights include Classic and Supreme pizzas generating the highest revenue and Medium and Large size pizzas being the most popular among customers.

Excel SQL Power BI
GitHub View Dashboard
04
Employee Project Management Analytics

I built an end-to-end Business Intelligence dashboard to track employee performance, departmental budgets, and project status across 5 business units with 10 employees and 10 projects. I designed a structured SQL relational database with 6 tables covering employees, departments, projects, assignments, and headshots, and wrote complex SQL queries using CTEs, UNION ALL, and multi-table JOINs to extract complete analytics data. I created an interactive Power BI dashboard with features like employee filter, department slicer, project status toggle, and automatic capital calculation per department. Key insights include the HR department being the only one with negative capital and Engineering having the highest available capital of $7,70,000.
